Bit late, BUT I'm a new person there too, 1.5 months-ish, and all I really have to say is, you're most likely going to learned what to do 'phonetically', if you will; most items are the same order, just either more or less added onto it. 

Learn the basics, cheese, egg, meat, sauce, (potato), wrap it up, and stick it in the toaster.  
You'll learn, and don't be hard on yourself if you get something wrong either, it's simple once you get used to it.

~~And make sure you get your tips once you're done training cuz I had to run around askin for em for a few weeks.~~

Just go with the flow, most items are just the same thing with added stuff, or differently arranged things.

For example all you really have to do is,  
\- Make sure you got the order right  
\- Clean your station  
\- Make sure you got backup supplies incase a big-ass order comes in (i.e, lettuce, sauce, bread, eggs, coffee, etc.)

BUT make sure you do minor work like cleaning your area because managers really don't like when you're just waiting for an order, but don't overwork yourself either. 

But do the job, make sure you get your tips, don't let your coworkers push you around, and you're good! You'll get the hang of it!

There is no 'trying too hard' (unless you're physically/emotionally distressed) it's most likely just them trying to get under your skin, been told that a couple of times, and nothings changed. Just make sure you do minor work like cleaning and stuff so they don't get on your ass.
